blocking_issues: FALSE GENERALISATION SHIPPED IN DOCUMENTATION. 'Three providers have now been measured and all three agree: perpetual is not free.' appears in docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md (line 618) and in apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/profiles/oracle.py (line 31). The repository's own data refutes it: FIVE distinct always_free (perpetual) offers classify Z0_TRUE_FREE under the real engine - github_actions_billing, github_packages_billing, github_codespaces_billing, cloudflare_pages_limits, cloudflare_workers_limits. GitHub is F008 slice P1, measured FIVE slices BEFORE Oracle, and tests/integration/test_ingest_github.py:244 asserts zero_cost_class == 'Z0_TRUE_FREE'. 'Three providers have now been measured' is also inaccurate on its face: six F008 providers are complete (github, vercel, gcp, aws, azure, oracle) and at least six have a perpetual offer. The claim is true only of the three cherry-picked providers named in the same sentence, and is stated as a general law. This is precisely the class the slice's own test docstring condemns: test_the_containers_rationale_says_which_document_carries_which_entry states 'A description that invites a false reading is a defect on this project even when it is literally true' - and this one is not literally true. NO Oracle verdict is affected and NO false-free claim results; the defect is a false NOT-free generalisation in shipped prose. Fix is two sentences in two files.
summary: Level-2 fresh-context evaluation of PR #73 (branch stsyg-oracle-provider-p6, head 85ef245dfce2df2aaac5a90db89f820dd6bbcf42, base main 741e1aab684fcf9dc9586aa119cc42d96de18083). Both SHAs re-derived with git ls-remote at start AND end of the evaluation; neither moved. All nine reported claims were independently re-derived and ALL NINE MATCHED, including the exact suite count (2657 passed / 2 skipped against a live PostgreSQL on an isolated port) and scripts/check.ps1 -NodeAudit ALL CHECKS PASSED at exit 0. The card reading was attacked hardest, as briefed, and it SURVIVES - strengthened by evidence the builder did not cite. Disposition is FAILED on ONE documentation defect only: a false generalisation ('perpetual is not free') shipped in docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md and the oracle.py docstring, refuted by the repository's own five Z0 perpetual offers across GitHub and Cloudflare. Every engineering claim, every Oracle verdict, the extraction integrity, the classification, the publication mechanism, the mutation battery, the positive control, the protected state and the append-only ledger are CORRECT and verified. No false-free claim exists anywhere in the slice.

acceptance_steps.name: reconciliation_both_directions_and_generator_refusals
acceptance_steps.acceptance_step: Pins/rows 24,6/6 - 7,0/0 - 8,0/0 - 7,0/0 - 6,0/0 - 8,0/0; generator refuses on zero/multiple needle matches, duplicate live block, table-row divergence.
acceptance_steps.method: Recomputed both numbers from the registered profile objects rather than reading the capture prose, then tested whether every block the capture calls 'pinned' is actually load-bearing by mutating it.
acceptance_steps.measured: Capture prose matches the reported numbers exactly (24/6, 7/0, 8/0, 7/0, 6/0, 8/0). BUT the recomputed count of DISTINCT asserted blocks is 24, 6, 7, 6, 5, 7 - one lower on five of six sources. Mechanism identified: the count includes the document <title>, and only oracle_always_free_resources actually pins its title as an assertion (scope='title'). MEASURED: mutating the <title> on the other five leaves extraction completely unaffected (error=None), while the same mutation on oracle_always_free_resources yields assertion_not_found. So 'all 7 pinned block(s)' describes 6 guards. See finding F2. The duplicate-block refusal is real and proven necessary: the block '50,000 Object Storage API requests per month' occurs exactly twice in the live parse, is retained twice in the capture, and pinning it yields ambiguous_assertion.

acceptance_steps.name: eleven_mutation_predictions
acceptance_steps.acceptance_step: 11 mutation predictions, 11 matched first run, including 3 false-positive controls.
acceptance_steps.method: Re-ran the parametrised battery and inspected the anchor mechanism for the 'a mutation that does not apply looks like a control that does not fire' trap.
acceptance_steps.measured: 11 passed, 180 deselected. Predictions are recorded in the parametrisation before the run. 8 rejection cases (assertion_deleted/reworded/truncated -> assertion_not_found; assertion_duplicated -> ambiguous_assertion; undeclared_matrix_row -> unknown_matrix_rows; mapped_row_removed -> missing_matrix_rows; renamed_tier -> table_not_found; duplicated_table -> ambiguous_table) plus 3 false-positive controls expecting None (extra_column, whitespace_entities, unrelated_paragraph_added). The trap is closed: _block_containing asserts the anchor matched EXACTLY ONE block and _mutate's once() asserts source.count(old) == 1, so a non-applying mutation raises loudly instead of passing silently.

acceptance_steps.name: the_card_reading_attacked_hardest
acceptance_steps.acceptance_step: Test the requires_card=True reading hard; confirm that rejecting it moves three offers Z1->UNKNOWN and produces no Z0 in either direction.
acceptance_steps.method: Fetched the LIVE oracle.com FAQ independently rather than re-reading the builder's quotation, then measured the counterfactual by re-classifying every Oracle offer with the card fact removed and with it forced to the OPPOSITE of the builder's reading.
acceptance_steps.measured: THE READING IS CORRECT, and corroborated by evidence the builder did not cite. The live FAQ presents the identity-verification block under its own question heading: 'Why do I need to provide credit or debit card information when I sign up for Oracle Cloud Free Tier?' - an explicit statement that a card IS needed to sign up for the FREE tier. The builder could not pin it (the collector does not capture those div containers, as its docstring discloses for the separate PAYG trap) and did not cite it, but it removes the ambiguity the builder honestly flagged. COUNTERFACTUAL, measured: rejecting ONLY the identity-verification block moves EXACTLY 3 offers Z1->UNKNOWN (oracle-always-free-services, oracle-cloud-free-tier, oracle-mysql-heatwave-always-free) - matching the brief's 'three' precisely; rejecting ONLY the 'most users' block moves 1 (oracle-free-tier). In EVERY scenario ANY Z0 = False. Stronger than claimed: even forcing requires_card=False on all six - the strongest possible reading against the builder - still yields UNKNOWN for all six and no Z0, because has_paid_dependencies is unknown on every Oracle source and gate 4 blocks Z0 independently. The disputed judgement provably cannot produce a false-free claim in either direction.

acceptance_steps.name: absence_based_refusals_attacked
acceptance_steps.acceptance_step: Attack the two absence-based refusals; verify test_an_absence_based_refusal_is_declared_as_such is non-vacuous.
acceptance_steps.method: Scanned the two documents BLOCK-WISE over the repository's own parsed blocks using a 12-term payment-instrument vocabulary, deliberately broader than the guard's two phrases ('credit card', 'credit/debit card').
acceptance_steps.measured: NO payment-instrument term found in ANY parsed block of oracle-always-free-resources or oracle-free-credit-promotion - searched for credit card, credit/debit card, debit card, payment card, payment method, payment verification, card, visa, mastercard, billing information, purchase, invoice. The absence is genuine and the refusal to import the requirement across documents is the honest call. The test is non-vacuous: it asserts the profile carries no requires_card assertion, asserts the normalised document contains no card phrase, drives the real extraction to confirm requires_card is None, and classifies to UNKNOWN with the matching blocking condition - it would fail if a card assertion were added or if the document acquired a card phrase. Correctly characterised as the structurally weaker shape: anything that later supplies the field flips it.

Cannot produce a false-free claim in either direction; both categories remain state=unknown.

evaluator_errors_self_reported: First baseline run reported 2415 passed / 244 skipped and I was one step from recording a discrepancy against the claimed 2657 / 2. The claim was right and I was wrong: I had installed only requirements-dev.txt, not apps/api/requirements.txt, and had no PostgreSQL. The two runs agreeing on 2659 COLLECTED is what exposed it - the disagreement was in my environment, not in the branch.

First scripts/check.ps1 run exited 1 and printed 'CHECKS FAILED: Prettier check, ESLint', which I could have recorded as a regression. Reading the tool's own stderr rather than the summary showed "'eslint' is not recognized" - node_modules was absent in my probe worktree. After npm ci the suite reported ALL CHECKS PASSED at exit 0. This is exactly the trap the brief named.

I hand-counted oracle_free_tier at 6 distinct pins against a claimed 7 and initially suspected a transcription error in the capture. Recomputing from the profile objects instead of by hand identified the real mechanism - an unpinned <title> included in the count - which is a narrower and more precise defect than the one I first assumed.

I initially counted 7 Z0 offers across the repository and had to correct to 5 DISTINCT offers: github 'unchanged' and 'changed' are document-case fixtures bound to the same github_actions_billing profile, not separate offers.
known_issues_or_risks: Absence-based refusals (oracle_always_free_resources, oracle_free_credit_promotion) are the structurally weaker shape and will flip to Z1 the moment either document acquires a payment statement. Correctly disclosed by the builder and asserted by test.
has_paid_dependencies is stated by no Oracle document and is claimed nowhere in either direction. This is the gate that makes the Oracle no-Z0 result robust to any reading of the card blocks.
The evaluation was run against the committed captures plus two independent live fetches of oracle.com and docs.oracle.com. Live pages can drift; the quotations verified verbatim on 2026-08-14/15.

recommendation: DO NOT MERGE AS-IS. One blocking defect, and it is a two-sentence documentation fix: delete or correct 'Three providers have now been measured and all three agree: perpetual is not free.' in docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md and apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/profiles/oracle.py, and the matching 'the third provider to demonstrate it' in tests/unit/test_adapter_oracle.py:256. An accurate replacement is available and is a stronger claim: Oracle's Always Free tier is genuinely perpetual by quotation AND card-gated by quotation on the same document, which is what makes it Z1 rather than Z0 - stated without generalising to providers whose perpetual offers this repository correctly publishes as Z0. Recommend also correcting the capture reconciliation wording so a counted <title> is not called a pinned block (F2), and refreshing current_contract.json measured_results after the rebase (F3). Everything else in this slice is verified correct: the six verdicts, the card reading, the absence refusals, the load-bearing positive control, the publication mechanism, the mutation battery, the protected state and the append-only ledger. No false-free claim exists anywhere in the slice, and the central product risk - Oracle marketed as 'Always Free' being published as Z0 - is correctly and provably refused. Re-evaluation after the prose fix should be cheap: no code, fixture or verdict changes are implied.
